when_to_use: When the system is showing an alarm/fault condition at the Hospital station and you need to identify the specific active alarm text/ID and its timestamp so the correct documented corrective action can be applied.

title: Remove A-Axis Gearbox (LOTO, side panel access, gripper removal, counter-balance handling)
summary: Safely remove the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox assembly by performing LOTO, removing the station side panel to access the motor, removing the gripper, and controlling counter-balance drift after gripper removal (either allow drift to the lower hard stop or remove the counter-balance weight).
when_to_use: Use when the OptiSweep A-axis gearbox must be removed and you need to follow the manual’s LOTO and disassembly sequence, including managing counter-balance drift risk after gripper removal.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute the physical disassembly steps (LOTO, side panel removal, gripper removal, gearbox unmounting/removal) and control counter-balance drift as specified.
safety_notes: Most fasteners in the A-axis gearbox have Loctite® 277™, so removal may be difficult (use appropriate tools and control unexpected movement).

After gripper removal, the system will be out of balance and the counter-balance will want to drift down; it is acceptable to allow drift to the lower hard stop or optionally remove the counter-balance weight to help balance the system.
If unexpected motion occurs during disassembly, stop and re-check LOTO.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the A-axis gearbox area
Tools: torque wrench, 4-mm hex wrench, 3/8-in. wrench/socket, standard screwdriver

external_references: Manual cross-reference: "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2 (referenced by the A-axis gearbox removal section).
Manual cross-reference: "Removal" on page 97 for gripper removal.

title: Use AGV API Controls to Remove/Recover an AGV and Pause/Resume All AGVs
summary: Use the System HMI API screen’s AGVs section to remove a problematic AGV by ID, recover (add back) the AGV by ID after physical recovery, and pause/resume all AGV movement fleet-wide.
when_to_use: When an AGV needs to be removed from the system (e.g., it has an issue) and later recovered after physical removal/recovery, and you need to pause/resume all AGV movement using the AGV API Controls.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for required physical removal/recovery steps after using Remove AGV (the AGV must be physically removed; if it has a tote, the tote must be taken to the hospital where the tote is removed).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute the AGV API Controls actions (Remove AGV, Recover AGV, Pause All AGVs, Resume All AGVs) and perform the required physical AGV/tote removal and recovery steps.
safety_notes: If the AGV has a tote, take the tote to the hospital where the tote is removed; the tote is recovered when it is put back in the system.
access_or_tools_needed: Hospital/onsite physical access to remove/recover the AGV and tote

title: Recover From AGV Fault During Exchange (RMS E-stop, remove faulted AGV, backfill, introduce new tote + empty AGV)
summary: Restore exchange flow after an AGV faults while leaving by stopping RMS, removing the faulted AGV from the RMS, optionally removing the trailing AGV if it does not backfill, then introducing a new tote and placing an empty AGV in the affected zone.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV faults during exchange while leaving and you need to restore exchange flow by removing the faulted AGV from RMS, handling backfill behavior, and reintroducing the correct tote + empty-AGV state in the affected zone.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute RMS stop (E-stop) and AGV removal/add actions via the RMS UI and the referenced AGV API Controls flow; verify backfill behavior and that the affected zone is re-established with a newly introduced tote and an empty AGV.
safety_notes: Perform an RMS E-stop as the first recovery action for this fault scenario.

access_required: rms_ui

steps.failure_condition: The trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described.

success_criteria: Faulted AGV is removed from RMS.

escalation_guidance: Escalate if the trailing AGV does not backfill and cannot be removed/cleared as described, or if the new tote/empty AGV cannot be introduced into the correct zone.

title: Recover an AGV After It Loses a Tote (No Fault) Using RMS and Hospital HMI
summary: Recover from the “AGV LOST TOTE NO FAULT” condition by stopping RMS, physically moving the AGV to the Hospital, removing and re-adding the AGV via the Hospital station PC/HMI workflow, power-cycling the AGV, re-localizing it by rolling over the Inbound Hospital Station QR code, then locating/removing the missing tote and adding it back into the system so the AGV can return the tote to the sorter.

safety_notes: E-stop RMS as the first action in this recovery sequence.

title: Recover Non-Recoverable Fault: AGV Stuck Using Operator Station HMI (Visu_ManControl → CellIO Status → OUT W1 forced value)
summary: On the operator station HMI, verify the non-recoverable AGV-stuck fault by confirming the selected tipper shows OUT Fault Status = 82 on the CellIO Status screen. Then force OUT W1 to either 3 (continue work) or 32771 (send the AGV to the hospital) by entering the value, checking the enable checkbox, waiting 10 seconds, and unchecking. Finally, press CYCLE START to restart operation.
when_to_use: Use when an AGV remains at the tipper after tote-tipping is complete (non-recoverable fault), and the operator station HMI indicates the AGV-stuck condition that requires forcing OUT W1 via the CellIO Status screen.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the HMI verification (Visu_ManControl → CellIO Status), select the stuck tipper, apply the documented OUT W1 forced value (3 or 32771) with the enable checkbox for 10 seconds, then uncheck and press CYCLE START.

title: Recover an AGV “BUMP” fault (Exception Codes 21057/21060) using RMS
summary: When RMS shows an AGV “Bump” fault with Exception Code 21057 or 21060, stop RMS, remove the obstruction that caused the bump/obstacle trigger, hold the AGV RESET button for two seconds to clear the fault, press E-stop again, then resume RMS. Verify the Exception Code is cleared on the RMS “Bump” Fault Screen before resuming normal operation.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when the RMS interface displays an AGV “Bump” fault and the Exception Code shown is 21057 or 21060, indicating a collision bar trigger or obstacle-avoidance trigger that requires RMS-side fault recovery.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for physical obstruction removal when the bump/obstacle trigger is caused by an on-grid obstruction; the obstruction must be physically cleared before attempting RESET.
Do not proceed to resume RMS if the Exception Code remains after the two-second AGV RESET attempt.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Execute RMS-side recovery actions (E-stop RMS, use AGV RESET for two seconds, press E-stop again, resume RMS) and verify the Exception Code is cleared on the RMS “Bump” Fault Screen.
safety_notes: This procedure includes E-stopping RMS (not physical E-stop).
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to remove the obstruction on the grid

title: Replace Flat-Flex Cable (FFC) at the A-axis PCA on a LOTOed tipper station
summary: Replace the flat-flex cable (FFC) connected to the A-axis PCA on a tipper station that has been LOTOed. Use the correct replacement part and ensure the correct left/right ClearLink controller hardware is installed (left/right are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses). The procedure removes the two FFC clamps (four M3 socket-head screws), unplugs/replugs the FFC, then reinstalls the clamps and the station side panel (nine self-tapping securing screws).
when_to_use: Use when you need to restore correct tipper station operation by replacing the flat-flex cable (FFC) connected to the A-axis PCA on a tipper station that is taken out of service via LOTO.
not_for: Do not proceed if you cannot confirm the correct left/right controller hardware for the tipper station (left/right ClearLink controllers are not interchangeable due to different IP addresses).
Do not proceed if the FFC cannot be unplugged/plugged cleanly or the clamps cannot be resecured with the four (4) M3 socket-head screws.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the LOTO and the physical hardware replacement steps (remove side panel, remove FFC clamps, unplug/plug FFC, reinstall clamps and side panel) using the specified tools and PPE.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).
Wear PPE: safety glasses, gloves.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the tipper station
4-mm hex wrench (listed in required tools for the section)
6-mm hex wrench (listed in required tools for the section)
LOTO capability for the tipper (per "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2)

system_preconditions: Tipper station is LOTOed before starting the replacement.

title: Remove OptiSweep Gripper at the Operator Station (LOTO + Disconnect Valve/Air/Cables)

title: Remove and Support Gripper for a Tipper Using Visu_MCP_Dual (Cycle Stop + Jog) and LOTO
summary: Prepare a tipper for gripper removal by stopping the current cycle, enabling manual jogging on the operator station HMI (Visu_MCP_Dual), positioning the gripper at the specified location, optionally supporting the carriages if the gripper is moved off home, and performing LOTO at the station e-panel. Confirm the correct gripper selection (left vs right) before proceeding.
when_to_use: Use when you must remove a tipper gripper and need to stop the cycle, jog the tipper/gripper to the required location, mechanically support the carriages if the gripper is moved from home, and apply LOTO at the station e-panel before removal.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a general tipper fault troubleshooting guide; it is specifically for gripper removal preparation (stop/jog/LOTO/left-right verification).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform HMI actions (CYCLE STOP, JOG, axis movement) and execute LOTO at the station e-panel as required for gripper removal preparation.
safety_notes: Caution: Components may be heavy. Use caution when lifting (gripper replacement section includes this caution).
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper operator station HMI access to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen
LOTO capability at the station e-panel ("Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" referenced by the manual)
Required tools for later removal: 2.5-mm, 3-mm, 5-mm, 6-mm hex wrenches; Loctite®

title: Recover Non-Recoverable Operator Station Motor Fault Using MCP_Dual (F3) Manual Jog, Reset, and Cycle Start
summary: When a non-recoverable operator station motor fault (e.g., motor overload) cannot be recovered in software, use the operator station HMI MCP_Dual screen (F3) to stop the cycle, enter manual jog mode, clear any axis faults with RESET, jog the correct axes to reposition the tote on/near the robot, then return to automatic mode and press CYCLE START to release the grippers and command the robot to the hospital station. After the robot leaves the tipper, press RESET.
when_to_use: Use this procedure when the operator station has a non-recoverable motor fault (example given: motor overload) and the station needs to be manually reset so the tote can be repositioned and the robot can be commanded to the hospital station.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute the MCP_Dual (F3) manual recovery sequence (CYCLE STOP, JOG, RESET, axis jogging, AUTO, CYCLE START, and final RESET).
access_or_tools_needed: Operator access to the operator station HMI
MCP_Dual screen (F3) controls: CYCLE STOP, JOG, RESET, AUTO, CYCLE START, and axis jog controls for Z1, Z2, A1, A2

system_preconditions: A non-recoverable operator station motor fault is present that requires manual reset (example: motor overload).

when_to_use: When you need to determine the current documented status of a tipper/station from the operator station stacklights (solid vs flashing colors, and horn alarm pattern when present).
not_for: Do not use this procedure to clear or reset E-stop or RMS error conditions.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Physically observe the operator station stacklights and interpret the solid/flashing color (and horn alarm pattern when present) into the documented tipper/station status.
safety_notes: If the observed stacklight pattern indicates E-stop activated (Solid Red), escalate immediately and do not attempt to clear remotely from this procedure.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the operator station stacklights
Ability to observe stacklight color(s), solid vs flashing, and horn alarm pattern (long vs intermittent) when present

access_required: Physical access to the operator station stacklights

visual_references.description: Stacklight state meanings (solid/flashing colors and RMS error/fault/AGV presence) used to interpret station status.

Operator station HMI Manual Control screen showing LAMP TEST behavior (audible alarm and stacklight flashing red) and tipper disable/fault reset controls for context while interpreting stacklight signals.
HMI context for Surepost tote indication (stacklight flashes white) and operator station controls (Surepost LEFT/RIGHT).

steps.title: Go to the affected operator station
steps.purpose: Ensure you are observing the correct stacklights for the tipper/station in question.
steps.instruction: Walk to the operator station for the affected tipper/station and position yourself so you can clearly see both stacklights.
steps.expected_result: You can visually identify both stacklights at the operator station for the affected tipper/station.
steps.healthy_condition: Both stacklights are visible and you can distinguish solid vs flashing behavior.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot clearly see one or both stacklights (blocked view, distance, or unclear flashing).

actions.label: Visually confirm stacklight visibility
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: Observe both stacklights and record solid vs flashing colors
steps.purpose: Capture the observable stacklight pattern that maps to the documented tipper/station status.
steps.instruction: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).
steps.expected_result: You have identified each stacklight’s state (solid/flashing) and color(s).
steps.healthy_condition: Stacklight colors and flashing behavior are unambiguous (e.g., solid blue vs flashing green, etc.).
steps.failure_condition: The stacklight pattern is unclear (e.g., intermittent visibility) or does not allow confident identification of solid vs flashing and color(s).

actions.label: Note stacklight state and color(s)
actions.exact_action: Observe both stacklights and note whether each is solid or flashing, and the displayed color(s).

steps.title: If horn alarm pattern is indicated, determine long vs intermittent horn during flashing
steps.purpose: Some documented stacklight patterns include horn alarm timing; capturing it improves status mapping accuracy.
steps.instruction: If the source indicates a horn alarm pattern for the flashing state you are seeing, also observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.
steps.expected_result: You have determined whether the horn alarm is long or intermittent during the flashing pattern.
steps.healthy_condition: Horn alarm timing is clearly distinguishable as long vs intermittent while the stacklight is flashing.
steps.failure_condition: Horn alarm timing cannot be distinguished (e.g., noise/unclear audio).

actions.label: Determine horn alarm timing
actions.exact_action: Observe whether there is a long horn alarm or intermittent horn alarm during the flashing pattern.

steps.title: Match the observed stacklight pattern to the documented tipper/station status meanings
steps.purpose: Convert the observed solid/flashing color (and horn timing when applicable) into the documented status.
steps.instruction: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings for tipper/station status, including RMS error, E-stop, tipping state, and surepost/bagout indications.
steps.expected_result: You can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color combination (and horn timing when present) to one documented status.
steps.healthy_condition: The observed pattern matches one of the documented combinations (examples include Solid Blue, Solid Green, Solid Red, Solid White, Solid Red+Yellow+Green, Flashing Blue, Flashing Green, Flashing Red, Flashing White, Flashing Yellow, and horn-timed combinations).
steps.failure_condition: The observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination.

actions.label: Map stacklight pattern to documented status
actions.exact_action: Match the observed pattern to the documented meanings: Solid Blue (Tipper paused), Solid Green (Tipping in process), Solid Red (Estop activated), Solid White (AGV present post-tipping), Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error), Flashing Blue (Tipper disabled), Flashing Green (Tipper starved), Flashing Red (Tipper faulted), Flashing White (SurePost tote being sent), Flashing Yellow (AGV present pre-tipping), Flashing Green+Yellow+Green with long horn alarm (Sort starting), Flashing White with intermittent horn alarm (Bagout complete).

stop_or_escalate_if: Observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination

steps.title: Stop and escalate for E-stop activated or RMS error
steps.purpose: Ensure critical conditions are handled appropriately and not cleared via this interpretation procedure.
steps.instruction: If the mapped status indicates E-stop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green), stop and escalate immediately.
steps.expected_result: You have identified whether the mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalated accordingly.
steps.healthy_condition: Mapped status is not Solid Red (E-stop activated) and not Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error).
steps.failure_condition: Mapped status is Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) and escalation is not initiated.

actions.label: Escalate critical condition
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the observed stacklight pattern indicates Estop activated (Solid Red) or RMS error (Solid Red+Yellow+Green).

stop_or_escalate_if: Solid Red indicates Estop is activated
Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error

success_criteria: Operator can map the observed stacklight solid/flashing color combination (and horn timing when present) to a documented tipper/station status.
Operator escalates immediately when the mapped status indicates Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error).
healthy_conditions: Stacklight pattern matches a documented combination and indicates a non-critical state (i.e., not Solid Red or Solid Red+Yellow+Green).
failure_conditions: Observed stacklight pattern does not match any documented combination.
Solid Red (E-stop activated) or Solid Red+Yellow+Green (RMS error) is present and escalation is not initiated.
escalation_guidance: If Solid Red indicates Estop is activated: escalate immediately; do not attempt to clear remotely from this procedure.
If Solid Red+Yellow+Green indicates an RMS error: escalate for further diagnostics.

Surepost tote indication: stacklight will flash white to let the operator know a Surepost tote is being delivered to the tipper.

title: Install Pneumatic Cylinder After Replacement (transfer fittings, bracket/rod end, reconnect air, reassemble, restart operator station)
summary: Reinstall a replaced pneumatic cylinder correctly so the lift plate rod end is pinned/retained, air lines are reconnected, covers/panels are reinstalled, and the operator station is restarted to resume normal operation.
when_to_use: Use this procedure after replacing a pneumatic cylinder when the cylinder must be reinstalled with the correct mechanical retention (rod end pin + retaining ring), air line reconnection, and reassembly, followed by restarting the operator station.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: performs the physical installation steps and restarts the operator station.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the pneumatic cylinder assembly
Hand tools for M6 socket head screws and M8 button-head screws
Tools to install pin and retaining ring
Ability to restart the operator station

access_required: Physical access to the pneumatic cylinder assembly
external_references: OptiSweep Operation and Maintenance Manual, section 7.3.10.2 Pneumatic Cylinder Installation (pages 151–153) and the referenced 'Starting The Operator Station' section on page 66

visual_references.description: Pneumatic cylinder assembly figure referenced by the pneumatic cylinder replacement/install section.

steps.title: Transfer air fittings and spherical rod end to the new cylinder
steps.purpose: Ensure the new cylinder has the correct air fittings and spherical rod end configuration before installation.
steps.instruction: Transfer the air fittings and the spherical rod end from the old cylinder to the new cylinder.
steps.expected_result: The new pneumatic cylinder has the air line fittings and spherical rod end installed/attached as transferred from the old cylinder.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line fittings and spherical rod end on the new cylinder match the transferred configuration from the old cylinder (no missing components).
steps.failure_condition: Air line fittings or the spherical rod end are not fully transferred/installed on the new cylinder.

actions.exact_action: Transfer the air fittings and spherical rod end from the old cylinder to the new cylinder.

steps.title: Mount cylinder bottom in bracket and install bracket half with two M6 screws
steps.purpose: Secure the cylinder mechanically in the bracket using the specified fasteners.
steps.instruction: Place the bottom of the cylinder in the bracket, then install the other half of the bracket using two (2) M6 socket head screws.
steps.expected_result: The cylinder bottom is seated in the bracket and the other half of the bracket is installed using two (2) M6 socket head screws.
steps.healthy_condition: Bracket halves are installed with exactly two (2) M6 socket head screws securing the cylinder in place.
steps.failure_condition: Cylinder bottom is not seated in the bracket or the bracket half is not secured with the two (2) M6 socket head screws.

actions.exact_action: Place the bottom of the cylinder in the bracket and install the other half of the bracket with the two (2) M6 socket head screws.

steps.healthy_condition: Pin and retaining ring are installed to retain the rod end between the lift plate brackets.
steps.failure_condition: Rod end cannot be fully seated between the lift plate brackets or the pin/retaining ring cannot be installed securely.

actions.exact_action: Slip the rod end between the brackets on the lift plate and insert the pin and retaining ring.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the rod end cannot be fully seated between the lift plate brackets or if the pin/retaining ring cannot be installed securely.

actions.exact_action: Reconnect the air lines.

title: Remove a Tipppper Pneumatic Cylinder (LOTO, side panel, gripper cover, air lines, retaining ring/pin, lower bracket screws)
summary: Safely remove the tipper pneumatic cylinder assembly for replacement by following the documented disassembly sequence and verifying the cylinder is released before removal.
when_to_use: Use when replacing the OptiSweep tipper pneumatic cylinder assembly and you need to remove it in the documented sequence (LOTO → side panel/gripper cover access → disconnect air lines → release lift plate via retaining ring/pin → remove lower bracket screws to free the cylinder).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform physical lockout/tagout and the disassembly steps in the specified order using the listed tools and fastener counts/sizes.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper before starting disassembly (manual references “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on page 2).
After removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin, the lift plate will drop a short distance—keep hands/feet clear of the drop path.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the tipper station
Loctite® (listed as required tool for the overall replacement context)

access_required: Physical access to the tipper station
system_preconditions: Tipper is placed under lockout/tagout (LOTO) before removing any covers or disconnecting air lines.
external_references: Manual section: 7.3.10.1 Pneumatic Cylinder Removal (Figure 7-10)

visual_references.description: Figure 7-10: Pneumatic cylinder assembly referenced by the pneumatic cylinder removal procedure (shows the pneumatic cylinder assembly and supports the removal sequence).

steps.title: Apply LOTO to the tipper
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is safely de-energized/locked out before any disassembly.
steps.instruction: Apply lockout/tagout (LOTO) to the tipper using the manual’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” method.
steps.expected_result: The tipper is locked out (LOTO applied) before proceeding to remove side panel/gripper cover components.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is in place and you can proceed with cover removal without needing to energize or actuate the tipper.
steps.failure_condition: You begin disassembly without LOTO, or LOTO cannot be confirmed as applied.

actions.label: Apply LOTO
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: If LOTO cannot be applied/confirmed, stop and do not proceed with cover removal or air line disconnection.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1: PNEUMATIC CYLINDER REMOVAL step 1: “LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).”

steps.title: Remove the station side panel (if needed) to access the motor
steps.purpose: Provide access to the gripper cover and pneumatic cylinder components.
steps.instruction: If necessary for access, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel, then remove the station side panel.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed (when needed) and the motor area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine (9) self-tapping side panel securing screws are removed and the side panel comes off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Side panel cannot be removed because screws are missing/incorrect, or fastener sizes/counts do not match the documented nine (9) self-tapping screws.

actions.label: Check access need
actions.exact_action: If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (nine self-tapping side panel screws).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1 step 2: “If necessary, use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.”

steps.title: Remove the gripper cover
steps.purpose: Expose the pneumatic cylinder and air line connections.
steps.instruction: Remove the gripper cover by removing the eight (8) M8 button head screws.
steps.expected_result: Gripper cover is removed and the pneumatic cylinder area is accessible.
steps.healthy_condition: All eight (8) M8 button head screws are removed and the cover comes off without forcing.
steps.failure_condition: Cover cannot be removed because screws are missing/incorrect, or fastener sizes/counts do not match the documented eight (8) M8 button head screws.

actions.label: Remove gripper cover screws
actions.exact_action: Remove the gripper cover by removing the eight (8) M8 button head screws.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (eight M8 gripper cover screws).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1 step 3: “Remove the gripper cover by removing the eight (8) M8 button head screws.”

steps.title: Disconnect the two air lines from the pneumatic cylinder
steps.purpose: Depressurize/disconnect pneumatic supply to allow safe release of the lift plate and cylinder removal.
steps.instruction: Remove the two (2) air lines from the pneumatic cylinder.
steps.expected_result: Both air lines are disconnected from the pneumatic cylinder.
steps.healthy_condition: Air line connections are fully disconnected (no remaining connected hoses/lines at the cylinder ports).
steps.failure_condition: Air lines cannot be removed, or connections do not separate as expected.

actions.label: Disconnect air lines
actions.exact_action: Remove the two (2) air lines from the pneumatic cylinder.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop/escalate if air lines cannot be removed.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1 step 4: “Remove the two (2) air lines from the pneumatic cylinder.”

steps.title: Release the lift plate by removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin
steps.purpose: Allow the lift plate to drop a short distance so the cylinder can be freed.
steps.instruction: At the rod end of the cylinder, remove one retaining ring and pull the pin releasing the lift plate; the lift plate will drop a short distance.
steps.expected_result: Lift plate releases and drops a short distance after removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin.
steps.healthy_condition: Lift plate visibly drops a short distance consistent with the procedure description.
steps.failure_condition: Lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin as described.

actions.label: Remove retaining ring and pull pin
actions.exact_action: At the rod end of the cylinder, remove one retaining ring and pull the pin releasing the lift plate which will drop a short distance.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin as described; re-check that the correct retaining ring and pin are removed before proceeding.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1 step 5: “At the rod end of the cylinder, remove one retaining ring and pull the pin releasing the lift plate which will drop a short distance.”

steps.title: Free the cylinder by removing the two lower bracket screws
steps.purpose: Detach the cylinder assembly from the lower bracket so it can be removed for replacement.
steps.instruction: At the bottom of the cylinder, remove two (2) M6 socket head screws to release half of the lower bracket and free the air cylinder.
steps.expected_result: Cylinder is freed after removing the two (2) M6 socket head screws (lower bracket released).
steps.healthy_condition: After removing both M6 socket head screws, the lower bracket releases as described and the cylinder can be freed without binding.
steps.failure_condition: Cylinder does not free after removing the two (2) M6 socket head screws, or fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes.

actions.label: Remove lower bracket screws
actions.exact_action: At the bottom of the cylinder, remove two (2) M6 socket head screws to release half of the lower bracket and free the air cylinder.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (two M6 socket head screws at bottom).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: 7.3.10.1 step 6: “At the bottom of the cylinder, remove two (2) M6 socket head screws to release half of the lower bracket and free the air cylinder.”

success_criteria: LOTO is applied to the tipper before disassembly.
Gripper cover is removed (eight (8) M8 button head screws removed).
Both air lines are disconnected from the pneumatic cylinder.
Lift plate releases and drops a short distance after removing the retaining ring and pulling the pin.
Cylinder is freed after removing the two (2) M6 socket head screws.
healthy_conditions: Lift plate drops a short distance after the retaining ring/pin action.
Fastener counts/sizes match the documented values at each removal point (nine side panel screws if removed; eight M8 gripper cover screws; one retaining ring/pin; two M6 lower bracket screws).
failure_conditions: Lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin as described.
Air lines cannot be removed.
Fasteners do not match documented counts/sizes at any step.
escalation_guidance: If the lift plate does not release after removing the retaining ring/pin, stop and re-check that the correct retaining ring and pin are removed before proceeding.

Escalate if air lines cannot be removed or if fasteners do not match the documented counts/sizes (nine self-tapping side panel screws, eight M8 gripper cover screws, one retaining ring/pin at rod end, two M6 socket head screws at bottom).

title: Apply Pneumatic LOTO at an Operator Station Shut-off Valve

when_to_use: Use when you need to isolate pneumatic power for a specific operator station by securing its pneumatic shut-off valve in the OFF position with LOTO.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the physical valve OFF action and apply LOTO to secure the OFF position for the targeted operator station.
safety_notes: Each operator station has its own pneumatic shut-off valve; ensure you isolate the correct station before applying LOTO.

LOTO hardware (lock and tag) appropriate for the site procedure

title: Remove Timing Belt on Tipper Station (A-axis/counterbalance positioning, LOTO, side panel removal, belt access)
summary: Safely prepare the OptiSweep tipper station for timing belt replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counterbalance between the actuator-base threaded holes, performing site “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” on the tipper, removing the nine (9) self-tapping side-panel fasteners to access the timing belt, and threading M6 socket-head screws into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.

not_for: Do not proceed to belt tension release unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent dropping.

safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper using the site’s “Operator Station Lockout/Tagout” process before removing side panels or accessing belt components.
Do not release belt tension unless the M6 socket-head screws are threaded into the holes below both carriages to prevent the A-axis/counterbalance from dropping.

title: Replace an OptiSweep Operator Station Tipper (LOTO, disconnect power/Ethernet/air, remove and reinstall)
summary: Safely replace a failed/replaced OptiSweep operator station tipper by performing LOTO, disconnecting the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), and air line (quick disconnect), removing the old tipper from the sub-plate, installing the new tipper onto the existing sub-plate, reconnecting conduit/power/air/Ethernet, and restarting the operator station.
when_to_use: Use when an OptiSweep operator station tipper must be removed and replaced, requiring LOTO and physical disconnection/reconnection of the tipper’s power (6-pin Molex), Ethernet (ClearLink controller), and air line (quick disconnect), followed by reinstall and operator station restart.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: performs LOTO and all physical disconnect/reconnect and mechanical removal/installation steps on the OptiSweep operator station tipper.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper before disconnecting power/air/Ethernet.
Use PPE: safety glasses and gloves.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the OptiSweep operator station tipper
Tools: 3/8-in. wrench or socket (if needed to remove nine (9) self-tapping securing screws for the station side panel)
Tools: hex head screwdriver/socket for the four (4) hex head screws holding the tipper to the sub-plate

access_required: Physical access to the OptiSweep operator station tipper
system_preconditions: Tipper is ready for LOTO (LOTO method referenced as "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

title: Inspect and Lubricate Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings (Grease Wetness on Z-Axis Linear Rails)
summary: Preventive maintenance for an OptiSweep tipper: visually inspect the Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease. If the rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks through the grease nipples using automotive bearing grease, applying 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block. Do not rely on wiping grease on the rails as a substitute for lubrication.
when_to_use: Use during tipper preventive maintenance to check Z-axis linear rail lubrication condition (wet grease vs dried grease) and to apply grease to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the visual inspection of both Z-axis linear rails and, if dry, lubricate the bearing blocks via the grease nipples with automotive bearing grease using the specified quantity per block.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to both Z-axis linear rails and the bearing blocks
Grease applicator capable of delivering 1.0 to 3.0 cc per bearing block

access_required: Physical access to both Z-axis linear rails and the bearing blocks

visual_references.description: End stop assembly diagram (included in packet artifacts; not specifically tied to grease nipple location for this procedure).

steps.title: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness or dried grease
steps.purpose: Determine whether lubrication is present (wet grease) or absent (dry/dried grease) to decide whether lubrication is required.
steps.instruction: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails and look for wet grease and/or signs of dried grease.
steps.expected_result: You can classify the condition of the Z-axis linear rails as either wet with grease or dry (not wet with grease) / showing dried grease.
steps.healthy_condition: Rails show grease wetness and/or signs of dried grease (indicating grease presence).
steps.failure_condition: Rails are dry (not wet with grease), indicating lubrication is needed.

actions.label: Inspect Z-axis rails
actions.exact_action: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease. If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

steps.title: If rails are dry, lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease
steps.purpose: Restore lubrication to the Z-axis bearing blocks when the rails are dry.
steps.instruction: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease), lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).
steps.expected_result: Grease is applied to the bearing blocks via the grease nipples using the specified quantity per block (1.0 to 3.0 cc per block).
steps.healthy_condition: Grease is applied to each bearing block through its grease nipples with 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block.
steps.failure_condition: Grease is not applied to the bearing blocks (or lubrication is attempted by wiping rails instead of greasing the bearing blocks).

actions.label: Lubricate bearing blocks
actions.exact_action: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

stop_or_escalate_if: If rails show signs of dried grease but lubrication cannot be performed as specified (e.g., inability to access nipples), stop and escalate to maintenance support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™).

steps.title: Locate the grease nipples on the two bearing blocks
steps.purpose: Ensure grease is applied to the correct lubrication points (the bearing blocks via the nipples).
steps.instruction: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).
steps.expected_result: You identify four (4) grease nipples total: two bearing blocks, one 1/4-in nipple on each end of each block.
steps.healthy_condition: All four nipples are located and accessible for greasing the bearing blocks.
steps.failure_condition: Nipples cannot be located or accessed, preventing lubrication as specified.

actions.label: Find grease nipples
actions.exact_action: Locate the grease nipples: there are two (2) bearing blocks, each with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end (four (4) nipples total).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the nipples to apply grease to the bearing blocks, stop and escalate to maintenance support.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: There are two (2) bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end each, so there are four (4) nipples to grease.

steps.title: Apply 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block
steps.purpose: Apply the specified grease quantity to ensure adequate lubrication of each bearing block.
steps.instruction: Using a grease applicator, add 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each bearing block (via its grease nipples).
steps.expected_result: Total grease applied per bearing block is within 1.0 to 3.0 cc, and grease has been delivered through the bearing block nipples.
steps.healthy_condition: Each bearing block receives 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease (four nipples total used to deliver grease to the two blocks).
steps.failure_condition: Grease quantity per block is outside 1.0 to 3.0 cc, or grease is not delivered to the bearing blocks through the nipples.

actions.exact_action: Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate.

success_criteria: Both Z-axis linear rails are inspected and classified as wet/dried or dry.
If rails are dry, grease is applied to each bearing block via the four (4) 1/4-in grease nipples with 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block.
Lubrication is performed via nipples; wiping grease on rails is not used as the lubrication method.
healthy_conditions: Rails show grease wetness and/or signs of dried grease.
After lubrication (when initially dry), grease is applied to each bearing block via the nipples with 1.0 to 3.0 cc per block.
failure_conditions: Rails are dry (not wet with grease) and bearing blocks are not lubricated via nipples.
Lubrication is attempted by wiping rails instead of greasing bearing blocks.
Rails show signs of dried grease but lubrication cannot be performed as specified due to inability to access nipples.
escalation_guidance: If lubrication cannot be performed as specified (e.g., inability to access nipples), stop and escalate to maintenance support.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Visually inspect both Z-axis linear rails for wetness of grease and/or signs of dried grease. If the rails are dry (not wet with grease) then lubricate the bearing blocks using automotive bearing grease (e.g., Mobil1™). There are two (2) bearing blocks with one standard 1/4-in nipple on each end each, so there are four (4) nipples to grease. Adding 1.0 to 3.0 cc of grease to each block should be adequate. title: Troubleshoot Too Many AGVs Directed to Hospital (Tipper Fault Beacon, Upstream Tipper Tote Count, E-stop)
summary: When too many AGVs are being directed to the hospital, check for a tipper fault using the operator station fault beacon and correct it, then return the tipper to service. safety_notes: If the upstream condition is confirmed as continuously sending at least five totes to the hospital station, push E-STOP and call a supervisor (per troubleshooting corrective action).

title: Remove Z-Axis Gearbox for OptiSweep Z-Axis Gearbox Replacement (A-axis jog + LOTO + side panel removal)
summary: Prepare the OptiSweep Z-axis for gearbox replacement by manually positioning the A-axis/counter-balance to the specified threaded-hole location using the tipper HMI, performing tipper lockout/tagout (LOTO), removing the station side panel (nine self-tapping fasteners), and exposing the motor/gearbox area. Install an M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
when_to_use: Use when preparing an OptiSweep Z-axis gearbox replacement and you must (1) position the A-axis/counter-balance between the actuator-base threaded holes, (2) lockout/tagout the tipper, and (3) remove the station side panel to access the motor/gearbox area.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a complete gearbox replacement workflow (it only covers the removal preparation steps evidenced in the provided manual section/page excerpt).
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the A-axis/counter-balance jog on the tipper HMI, execute tipper LOTO using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure, remove the nine side-panel fasteners, remove the station side panel, and install the M6 socket-head screw below both carriages.
safety_notes: Perform tipper LOTO using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
Stop if the A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned as described or cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to tipper station for LOTO and side panel removal

access_required: tipper_hmi (WebVisu/VISU operator station HMI)
Physical access to the tipper station
system_preconditions: Tipper is capable of manual jog positioning of the A-axis and counter-balance via the tipper HMI.
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure on page 2 (referenced by the manual for tipper LOTO).

visual_references.description: Figure 7-7: Gearbox diagram supporting the removal preparation steps (A-axis/counter-balance positioning, tipper LOTO reference, nine side-panel fasteners, and M6 socket-head screw below both carriages).

steps.title: Jog A-axis and counter-balance to the threaded-hole position
steps.purpose: Position the A-axis/counter-balance so the gearbox removal preparation can proceed safely and so the carriages can be secured to prevent dropping after belt tension is released.
steps.instruction: On the tipper HMI (WebVisu/VISU), manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base. There are two holes adjacent to each rail; position the carriages between the holes on the respective rails.
steps.expected_result: A-axis/counter-balance are positioned between the threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
steps.healthy_condition: Carriages are visibly located between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail (as shown in the gearbox figure).
steps.failure_condition: A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described, or carriages cannot be placed between the holes on their respective rails.

actions.label: Manual jog A-axis/counter-balance
actions.exact_action: Use the HMI to manually position (jog) the A-axis and counter-balance between the threaded holes in the actuator base.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.

steps.title: Perform tipper LOTO using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure
steps.purpose: Ensure the tipper is locked out/tagged out before removing the station side panel and accessing the motor/gearbox area.
steps.instruction: Perform LOTO for the tipper using the manual’s referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure (page 2).
steps.expected_result: Tipper is locked out/tagged out.
steps.healthy_condition: LOTO is completed for the tipper per the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
steps.failure_condition: LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.

actions.label: Execute tipper lockout/tagout
actions.exact_action: LOTO the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" procedure.

steps.title: Remove the station side panel fasteners and the station side panel
steps.purpose: Expose the motor/gearbox access area by removing the station side panel secured with nine self-tapping fasteners.
steps.instruction: Using a 3/8-in. wrench or socket, remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel, then remove the station side panel to access the motor.
steps.expected_result: Station side panel is removed and the motor/gearbox access area is exposed.
steps.healthy_condition: All nine self-tapping fasteners are removed and the station side panel is removed without remaining fasteners attached.
steps.failure_condition: Fasteners cannot be removed with the 3/8-in. wrench/socket, or the side panel cannot be removed to access the motor.

actions.label: Remove side panel fasteners
actions.exact_action: Use a 3/8-in. wrench or socket to remove the nine (9) self-tapping securing the side panel then remove the station side panel to access the motor.

steps.title: Install M6 socket-head screw below both carriages to prevent dropping
steps.purpose: Prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released during subsequent gearbox removal steps.
steps.instruction: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages. These fasteners prevent the A-axis and counter-balance from dropping once belt tension is released.
steps.expected_result: An M6 socket-head screw is installed into the holes below both carriages.
steps.healthy_condition: M6 socket-head screw(s) are seated in the holes below both carriages, providing mechanical retention as described.
steps.failure_condition: M6 socket-head screw cannot be inserted into the holes below both carriages, or the carriages cannot be held in place.

actions.label: Insert M6 screw below carriages
actions.exact_action: Insert an M6 socket-head screw into the holes below both carriages.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the carriages cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.

success_criteria: A-axis/counter-balance are positioned between the threaded holes with carriages between the holes on their respective rails.
Tipper is locked out/tagged out using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
Station side panel is removed and the motor/gearbox access area is exposed.
M6 socket-head screw is installed below both carriages to prevent dropping once belt tension is released.
healthy_conditions: Carriages are between the two threaded holes adjacent to each rail.
LOTO is completed for the tipper per the referenced procedure (page 2).
Side panel removal exposes the motor/gearbox access area.
M6 socket-head screw is installed below both carriages.
failure_conditions: A-axis/counter-balance cannot be positioned between the threaded holes as described.
LOTO cannot be completed safely using the referenced Operator Station Lockout/Tagout procedure (page 2).
Side panel cannot be removed to access the motor.
Carriages cannot be held in place with the M6 socket-head screw.
escalation_guidance: If any stop condition is met (positioning, LOTO, side panel removal, or M6 screw retention), stop work and escalate per site maintenance escalation process (not specified in the provided packet).

title: Quick Replacement of Z-Axis Cable Carrier (Snap Apart/Ends Snap-In)
summary: Performs a quick Z-axis cable carrier replacement by LOTO the tipper, snapping the carrier apart at both ends, removing the old carrier, installing the new carrier, snapping cross bars closed, and snapping both ends into the end pieces that remain mounted.
when_to_use: Use when both ends of the existing Z-axis cable carrier are in good condition and you need a quick replacement by snapping the carrier apart at both ends, leaving the end pieces mounted on the tipper.
not_for: Do not use this quick replacement method if either end of the existing carrier is not in good condition (the procedure is explicitly a quick replacement only when both ends are good).
Do not proceed if LOTO cannot be completed safely or if access to the motor/side panel is unclear.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform LOTO on the tipper and execute the physical cable carrier replacement steps (side panel removal if necessary, snap-apart/snap-in actions, and reassembly).
safety_notes: Perform LOTO on the tipper before removing the side panel or disassembling the cable carrier.
access_or_tools_needed: Physical access to the tipper and station side panel

access_required: physical_floor
system_preconditions: Both ends of the existing Z-axis cable carrier are in good condition (required for quick replacement).
Tipper can be safely LOTO.

title: Configure Barcode Interface scanner settings (password, prefixes, HTTP/OPC URLs) for AGV and Hospital control IPs
summary: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, update the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner’s Barcode Interface settings so tote/location label prefixes match and the HTTP/OPC URLs point to the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses, then save the settings.
when_to_use: Use when a scanner is replaced and the new scanner must be set up so Barcode Interface settings use the correct tote/location prefixes and the correct AGV/Hospital control IP addresses in the HTTP and OPC URL fields.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the Barcode Interface settings update (enter password, verify prefixes, update HTTP/OPC URLs, save settings).

access_required: FORTNA account login on the Windows laptop
system_preconditions: Network connectivity from the laptop to both the AGV control and Hospital control (validated by ping per scanner setup requirements).
Barcode Interface application is installed on the Windows laptop (found on the desktop with a FORTNA logo).

visual_references.description: Scanner Setup screen showing the settings button/password prompt, prefix fields, HTTP URL field (AGV control IP), OPC URL field (Hospital control IP), and Save Settings button.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface on the scanner setup laptop
steps.purpose: Open the application used to configure the replacement scanner settings.
steps.instruction: On the Windows laptop used for scanner setup, launch the Barcode Interface application (Barcode Interface.exe).
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and ready for interaction (scanner setup workflow visible).
steps.healthy_condition: The application is running and you can proceed to the settings area.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or is not accessible on the desktop.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Open Settings and enter the default password
steps.purpose: Access the protected settings panel to edit prefixes and HTTP/OPC URLs.
steps.instruction: In Barcode Interface, click the "settings" button and supply the default password "Opti".
steps.expected_result: The settings panel accepts the password and the settings fields are available for editing.
steps.healthy_condition: You can view/edit the prefix configuration fields and the HTTP/OPC URL fields.
steps.failure_condition: Password is rejected or settings fields do not become available.

actions.label: Open settings
actions.exact_action: Check the settings by clicking the settings button, supply the password. By default, the pass- word is “Opti”.

steps.title: Verify tote/location label prefixes match
steps.purpose: Ensure the scanner will interpret labels correctly for totes and locations.
steps.instruction: Verify the configured prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.
steps.expected_result: Prefix values shown in the settings match the tote/location label prefixes you physically verify.
steps.healthy_condition: Prefixes match the tote/location labels (no mismatch observed).
steps.failure_condition: Prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.

actions.label: Compare prefixes
actions.exact_action: Verify prefixes match the labels on the totes and locations.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the prefixes do not match the tote/location labels.

steps.title: Update HTTP and OPC URLs to correct AGV/Hospital control IPs
steps.purpose: Point the scanner interface to the correct AGV control and Hospital control endpoints.
steps.instruction: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC settings so the HTTP URL contains the AGV control IP address and the OPC URL contains the Hospital control IP address.
steps.expected_result: HTTP URL field includes the AGV control IP address; OPC URL field includes the Hospital control IP address.
steps.healthy_condition: Both URL fields contain the correct IP addresses in the expected HTTP vs OPC fields.
steps.failure_condition: HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.

actions.label: Edit HTTP/OPC URLs
actions.exact_action: Change the URL for both the HTTP and OPC setting to contain the AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses respectively.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the HTTP/OPC URLs cannot be updated to include the correct AGV control and Hospital control IP addresses.

steps.title: Save the scanner settings
steps.purpose: Commit the updated prefixes and URLs so the scanner uses them.
steps.instruction: Save the settings using the "Save Settings" button.
steps.expected_result: Settings are saved (the updated prefix/URL values are committed after clicking "Save Settings").
steps.healthy_condition: After saving, the settings reflect the updated prefixes and the HTTP/OPC URLs with the correct IP addresses.
steps.failure_condition: Settings do not save or the displayed values revert/are not updated after saving.

actions.exact_action: Save the settings with the "Save Settings" button.

title: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner using Barcode Interface (hardware connect + connectivity + calibration)
summary: Set up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner so the Barcode Interface application shows healthy connectivity and the scanner is calibrated when the app connectivity indicator is red.
when_to_use: Use when a Zebra DS3608-SR scanner has been replaced and needs setup so Barcode Interface connectivity is healthy; if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator is red, calibration is required.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the scanner dock/cabling connection, launch Barcode Interface, verify the connectivity indicator, and run calibration when the indicator is red.
access_or_tools_needed: USB cable with RJ45 side (to dock) and USB to laptop
Network connectivity to the AGV control and Hospital control at the laptop (validated by pinging their IP addresses)

access_required: FORTNA account login on the Windows laptop
system_preconditions: Barcode Interface.exe is installed on the Windows 10/11 laptop (found on the desktop with a FORTNA logo).
Scanner dock, USB cable, and power adapter are available for the replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner.
Laptop has network connectivity to the AGV control and Hospital control (validated by pinging their IP addresses).

visual_references.description: Scanner Setup procedure image (hardware connections + dock power light + battery indicator note + connectivity/calibration decision).

steps.title: Verify laptop and Barcode Interface availability; log in with a FORTNA account
steps.purpose: Ensure the setup laptop can run Barcode Interface and is authenticated before connecting and configuring the scanner.
steps.instruction: On the Windows 10/11 laptop, confirm Barcode Interface.exe is installed (on the desktop with a FORTNA logo), then log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.
steps.expected_result: You are logged into the Windows laptop with a FORTNA account and Barcode Interface.exe is available to launch.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is present on the desktop and you can proceed to launch it.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface.exe is not available or you cannot log in with a FORTNA account.

actions.label: Confirm Barcode Interface.exe and login
actions.exact_action: Log into the laptop with a FORTNA account.

steps.title: Connect scanner dock cabling and power; confirm dock lights up
steps.purpose: Provide power and connectivity path from the scanner dock to the laptop so the scanner can charge and Barcode Interface can detect connectivity.
steps.instruction: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, connect the USB to the laptop, and connect the auxiliary cable to the power adapter. Plug the power adapter into a 120 VAC outlet (x2). Confirm the dock lights up.
steps.expected_result: The scanner dock powers on and its lights are on.
steps.healthy_condition: Dock lights up after the power adapter is plugged into a 120 VAC outlet.
steps.failure_condition: Dock does not light up after connecting power.

actions.label: Connect RJ45/USB/aux power
actions.exact_action: Connect the RJ45 side of the USB cable to the back of the scanner dock, the USB to the laptop, and the auxiliary to the power adapter. Be sure to plug the adapter into a 120 VAC outlet. The dock should light up.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the dock does not light up after connecting power.

steps.title: Charge the scanner on the dock until the battery indicator turns green
steps.purpose: Ensure the replacement scanner has sufficient charge before proceeding to Barcode Interface connectivity checks and calibration.
steps.instruction: If the scanner is uncharged, place it on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.
steps.expected_result: Scanner battery indicator changes from red to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Battery indicator on top of the scanner is green.
steps.failure_condition: Battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.

actions.label: Check battery indicator color
actions.exact_action: If the scanner is uncharged it will need to rest on the dock until the red battery symbol shown on top turns green.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.

steps.title: Launch Barcode Interface application
steps.purpose: Open the application that displays connectivity status and provides the calibration action when connectivity is red.
steps.instruction: Launch the Barcode Interface application (should be on the desktop).
steps.expected_result: Barcode Interface is open and the screen is ready for connectivity status verification.
steps.healthy_condition: Barcode Interface window is visible and you can view the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the screen.
steps.failure_condition: Barcode Interface does not launch or the connectivity indicator is not visible.

actions.label: Open Barcode Interface
actions.exact_action: Launch the Barcode Interface application. This should be on the desktop.

steps.title: Check Barcode Interface connectivity indicator (bottom right)
steps.purpose: Determine whether the scanner needs calibration based on the app connectivity status.
steps.instruction: Check the connectivity indicator at the bottom right of the Barcode Interface screen.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is either green or red.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red.

actions.label: Observe connectivity indicator
actions.exact_action: Check connectivity on the bottom right of the screen.

steps.title: Calibrate scanner only if connectivity indicator is red
steps.purpose: Restore healthy scanner connectivity by running calibration when the app reports red connectivity.
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions until calibration completes.
steps.expected_result: After calibration, the operator observes the connectivity indicator change to green.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator becomes green after calibration.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.

actions.label: Run calibration
actions.exact_action: If red, click "Calibrate Scanner" and follow the onscreen instructions.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following the onscreen instructions.

steps.title: Skip calibration if connectivity indicator is green
steps.purpose: Avoid unnecessary calibration when the scanner already reports healthy connectivity.
steps.instruction: If the connectivity indicator is green, skip calibration and proceed to the next step of the overall scanner setup procedure.
steps.expected_result: Connectivity indicator is green and calibration is not performed.
steps.healthy_condition: Connectivity indicator is green.
steps.failure_condition: Connectivity indicator is not green (red) but calibration is skipped.

actions.label: Confirm green status
actions.exact_action: If green, skip this step.

success_criteria: Barcode Interface connectivity indicator at the bottom right is green.
If connectivity was red initially, calibration was run and the operator observes the connectivity indicator change to green.
Scanner battery indicator is green (if it was initially red).
healthy_conditions: Scanner dock lights up after power is connected.
Scanner battery indicator turns green after charging on the dock.
Barcode Interface connectivity indicator at bottom right is green.
failure_conditions: Dock does not light up after connecting power.
Scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock.
Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after clicking "Calibrate Scanner" and following onscreen instructions.
escalation_guidance: If the dock does not light up after connecting power, stop and escalate.
If the scanner battery indicator does not turn green after resting on the dock, stop and escalate.
If the Barcode Interface connectivity indicator remains red after calibration, stop and escalate.

title: Check SMALLS System Health Using the Smalls Overview HMI Screen (Color-Coded Layout)
summary: Use the SMALLS overview screen on the System HMI to quickly identify which parts of the SMALLS system are in a normal vs abnormal (color-coded) status based on the system layout.
when_to_use: When you need a fast, at-a-glance health check of the SMALLS system parts using the color-coded SMALLS system layout.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Open the System HMI SMALLS overview screen and identify any parts showing abnormal color-coded status; stop/escalate when abnormal indications are widespread or unclear.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU (System HMI access where the SMALLS button is available)

steps.failure_condition: The "Smalls" overview screen does not open or the SMALLS layout is not visible.

actions.label: Press SMALLS

steps.title: Review the SMALLS system layout on the "Smalls" overview screen

steps.instruction: On the "Smalls" overview screen, review the SMALLS system layout.

actions.label: Review layout

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

steps.title: Check each SMALLS part’s color-coded status indicator
steps.purpose: Determine which parts are abnormal by observing the color-coded status indicators on the layout.
steps.instruction: For each part shown on the layout, observe the color-coded status indicator.
steps.expected_result: You have identified which parts (if any) show abnormal color-coded status (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part).

steps.failure_condition: One or more parts show abnormal color-coded status indicators.

steps.title: Identify abnormal parts and decide whether to stop/escalate
steps.purpose: Ensure abnormal indications are handled appropriately and escalate when abnormality is widespread or unclear.
steps.instruction: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition (i.e., not the normal/expected color for that part). If the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, treat it as abnormal.

steps.healthy_condition: No parts indicate abnormal color-coded status; no offline/blocked section is indicated.
steps.failure_condition: Multiple parts show abnormal color-coded status, or the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action, or you cannot determine which parts are abnormal.

actions.label: Identify abnormal parts
actions.exact_action: Identify any parts whose color-coded status indicates an abnormal condition.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if multiple system parts show abnormal color-coded status.
Stop and escalate if the layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.
Stop and escalate if you cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The "Smalls" overview screen shows the smalls system layout and a color-coded status of each part of the system.

The operator cannot determine which parts are abnormal from the screen.
The layout indicates an offline/blocked section requiring support action.

success_criteria: Process Status indicators on VISU_DATA show the expected green meanings for the intended action.
SEND LEFT TO HOSPITAL or SEND RIGHT TO HOSPITAL is used only when the intended tipper state is consistent with the Process Status indicators.
PAUSE TIPPER is used to pause both tippers when needed.
healthy_conditions: In Cycle indicator is green when the tipper is operating in Auto mode.
Tipper Ready indicator is green when ready to receive a tote.
AGV Present indicator is green when a robot is currently stationed at the tipper.
Tip in Process indicator is green when the gripper takes hold of a tote and remains green until the tote is released.
Tipper Clear indicator is green when the gripper is open.
Tipper Faulted indicator is green if the tipper currently has a fault.
failure_conditions: Process Status indicators do not match the expected green states for the intended action (e.g., tipper not ready / not in the expected state).
Tipper Faulted indicator is green when you are attempting an action that requires a non-faulted state (mismatch between intended action and observed indicator state).
escalation_guidance: If the Process Status indicators do not show the expected green states for the action you are attempting (e.g., tipper not ready / faulted state not reflected), stop using the send/pause controls and escalate per site procedure.

title: Verify Tipper Axis Referencing and Motion Indicators on Visu_MCP_Dual (A1/Z1/A2/Z2)
summary: On the tipper operator HMI screen Visu_MCP_Dual, verify that the left (A1/Z1) and right (A2/Z2) gripper axes show the correct referencing indicator (green 'R' circle) and determine whether an axis is currently moving (yellow data field). An axis that is out of reference may contribute to a tipper fault.
when_to_use: Use when investigating a tipper fault and you need to confirm whether the left/right tipper axes are referenced and whether an axis is currently moving based on the Visu_MCP_Dual indicators.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Navigate to the Visu_MCP_Dual screen and read the axis position values and referencing/motion indicators.
safety_notes: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen includes movement controls; the manual jog function is intended for maintenance personnel (do not jog unless you are authorized/qualified per site practice).

access_required: Access to the operator station tipper HMI to view Visu_MCP_Dual

visual_references.description: Visu_MCP_Dual (Operator Station Control Panel) showing the primary operator interface and cycle indicators for axis referencing.

steps.title: Open the primary tipper operator screen Visu_MCP_Dual
steps.purpose: Get to the screen that displays the left/right axis position boxes (A1/Z1 and A2/Z2) and the cycle referencing indicator ('R').

steps.healthy_condition: A1 and Z1 values are present and readable in the left gripper axis boxes.
steps.failure_condition: A1/Z1 values are missing, not updating when the system is moving, or the fields are not visible.

steps.expected_result: The cycle referencing indicator shows green 'R' when the axis has been referenced.
steps.healthy_condition: The 'R' circle is green, indicating the axis has been referenced.
steps.failure_condition: The 'R' circle is not green (axis not referenced) while you are investigating a tipper fault.

actions.label: Verify green 'R' circle
actions.exact_action: Check whether the circle is green; if the circle is green, the axis has been referenced.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the axis referencing indicator does not show referenced (green 'R' rule) while the system is faulting.

steps.title: Observe whether the axis data field is yellow (axis in motion)
steps.purpose: Determine whether an axis is currently moving based on the yellow data field indicator.
steps.instruction: On Visu_MCP_Dual, observe the axis data field color; confirm whether it is yellow (indicating the axis is in motion).
steps.expected_result: The data field is yellow when the axis is in motion.
steps.healthy_condition: If the system is not actively moving the axis, the data field is not yellow; if it is moving, it appears yellow.
steps.failure_condition: The data field color behavior does not match the expected referenced/motion indicators during the fault investigation (e.g., unexpected lack of motion indication when motion is occurring, or unexpected motion indication when the system should be idle).

actions.label: Check yellow motion indicator
actions.exact_action: Observe whether the data field is yellow when the axis is in motion.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the screen behavior does not match the expected referenced/motion indicators.

steps.title: Interpret out-of-reference condition as a potential contributor to tipper fault
steps.purpose: Use the screen’s referencing rule to identify an out-of-reference condition that may contribute to a tipper fault.
steps.instruction: If the axis is out of reference (i.e., the green 'R' circle rule is not satisfied), note that an out-of-reference axis may cause a tipper fault.
steps.expected_result: You have identified whether the axis is out of reference based on the cycle 'R' indicator rule, and you can state that this condition may contribute to a tipper fault.
steps.healthy_condition: The axis is referenced (green 'R' circle) when investigating a fault, or the out-of-reference condition is not present.
steps.failure_condition: The axis is out of reference (not referenced per the green 'R' rule) during a fault investigation.

actions.label: Note out-of-reference condition
actions.exact_action: If the axis is out of reference (not referenced per the screen’s green 'R' rule), note that an out-of-reference axis may cause a tipper fault.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the axis referencing indicator does not show referenced (green 'R' rule) while the system is faulting.

success_criteria: A1/Z1 and A2/Z2 position values (in steps) are visible and readable on Visu_MCP_Dual.
The cycle referencing indicator follows the rule: green 'R' indicates the axis has been referenced.
The axis data field shows yellow when the axis is in motion.
healthy_conditions: Green 'R' circle indicates referenced axis status.
Yellow data field appears only when the axis is in motion.
failure_conditions: Referencing indicator does not show referenced (green 'R' rule not satisfied) while the system is faulting.
Screen behavior does not match expected referenced/motion indicators.
escalation_guidance: If the axis is out of reference (green 'R' rule not satisfied) while the system is faulting, stop and escalate for further troubleshooting.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Item 10: A1/Z1 show current position (in steps) for left gripper; A2/Z2 show current position (in steps) for right gripper. The 'R' in the cycle denotes whether the axis has been referenced: if the circle is green, the axis has been referenced. The data field will be yellow when the axis is in motion. An axis being 'out of reference' may cause a tipper fault.
F3 navigates to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen; NOTE: this will be the primary screen that operators need to use.

missing_details: The packet does not provide explicit per-axis mapping of the yellow motion indicator to A1 vs Z1 vs A2 vs Z2; it only states that the data field will be yellow when the axis is in motion.
The packet does not provide explicit UI labels for the exact location/label of the yellow data field beyond the general rule; operators should rely on the visible color change on Visu_MCP_Dual.

title: Restart Tipper Cycle After Fault or E-Stop Using Visu_MCP_Dual Buttons
summary: Use the primary operator HMI screen "Visu_MCP_Dual" (Tipper Machine Control Panel) to reset the tipper system after a fault (RESET → CYCLE START) or after an E-stop (ESTOP RESET → AUTO → CYCLE START). Active buttons are indicated by illuminated green bars.
when_to_use: When the tipper system needs to be reset and the tipper operation cycle restarted after a fault or after an E-stop, using the primary operator screen "Visu_MCP_Dual".
not_for: Do not use this procedure to jog the tipper. The screen notes that only maintenance personnel should jog the tipper.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the RESET / ESTOP RESET and AUTO / CYCLE START button sequence on the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen and verify the expected restart behavior.
safety_notes: Only maintenance personnel should jog the tipper (JOG is maintenance-only per the screen description).

title: Use VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” to copy axis parameters to the selected axis
summary: On the Operator Station HMI (VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen), use the VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” button to copy Machine Data parameters from the opposite tipper to the selected axis (Z1, A1, Z2, or A2).
when_to_use: Use when you need to update VISU_MDS Machine Data parameters for a selected axis by copying the corresponding parameters from the other tipper using the VISU_MDS “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” function.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for motor replacement commissioning/alignment steps; the manual states Machine Data parameters generally do not require changing unless a motor is replaced.
