steps.title: Verify the selected axis Machine Data values updated
steps.purpose: Confirm the copy operation updated the expected Machine Data IDs/fields for the selected axis.
steps.instruction: On the VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen, verify that the Machine Data values for the selected axis updated to the copied values. Check the listed IDs/fields including: OT Minus (ID 1), Tote Pickup Position (ID 5), travel opposite positions (IDs 6 and 7), Tote Dump Position (ID 8), Soft Travel Lim Pos (ID 9), OT Pos (ID 10), Base Speed for AutoCycle (ID 11) and Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (ID 12), Jog Speed (ID 13) and Jog Acceleration (ID 14), and Home/offset/homing parameters (IDs 20–24).
steps.expected_result: The selected axis shows updated values for the checked Machine Data IDs/fields after the copy.
steps.healthy_condition: The Machine Data values for the selected axis reflect the copied parameters from the other tipper for the parameters that should match machine-to-machine (with the manual-stated exceptions).
steps.failure_condition: One or more of the checked Machine Data IDs/fields do not change as expected after the copy, or mismatches persist after copy.

stop_or_escalate_if: If mismatches persist after copy, re-check the axis selection and the specific Machine Data IDs shown on VISU_MDS.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: From machine to machine, the following data values should match: ID 1 OT Minus; ID 5 Tote Pickup Position; ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position; ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position; ID 8 Tote Dump Position; ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos; ID 10 OT Pos; ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle; ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle; ID 13 Jog Speed; ID 14 Jog Acceleration; and ID 20 Home Position; ID 21 Home Offset; ID 22 Homing Speed; ID 23 Homing CAM Speed; ID 24 Homing Acceleration.
Exceptions for matching values: MD5 Tote Pickup Position will be unique for every machine and every axis; MD21 Home Offset will be unique for every machine and every axis.

success_criteria: After pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE”, the VISU_MDS Machine Data values for the selected axis reflect the copied parameters from the opposite tipper.

The checked Machine Data IDs/fields on VISU_MDS show updated values consistent with the manual’s machine-to-machine matching list, accounting for the stated exceptions (MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset).
healthy_conditions: VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen shows axis parameters for Z1, A1, Z2, and A2.
After “COPY FROM OPPOSITE”, the selected axis Machine Data values update (for the parameters intended to match machine-to-machine).
MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset are treated as exceptions (unique per machine and axis) when evaluating whether values match.
failure_conditions: Pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” produces no visible change to the selected axis Machine Data values.
After copy, one or more expected Machine Data IDs/fields do not update or remain mismatched (excluding the manual-stated exceptions).
escalation_guidance: Stop and escalate if pressing “COPY FROM OPPOSITE” results in no visible change to the selected axis Machine Data values.
If mismatches persist after copy, re-check the axis selection and the specific Machine Data IDs shown on VISU_MDS, then escalate if still unresolved.

title: Verify VISU_MDS (Machine Data) axis parameters match between machines (Z1/A1/Z2/A2)
summary: Use the Operator Station HMI VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen to verify that key axis parameters match between machines for axes Z1, A1, Z2, and A2. Treat MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) as documented exceptions that are expected to be unique per machine and per axis.
when_to_use: When you need to confirm whether VISU_MDS “Machine Data” axis parameters are consistent between machines for the same axis (Z1/A1/Z2/A2), using the documented matching rules and exceptions.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Open the Operator Station HMI VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen and compare Machine Data values between machines for the selected axis.
safety_notes: The VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen parameters generally do not require changing unless a motor is replaced.
access_or_tools_needed: Tipper HMI / WebVisu / VISU access to the VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen

system_preconditions: VISU_MDS “Machine Data” screen is available on the Operator Station HMI

steps.title: Compare machine-to-machine values for the selected axis (Z1/A1/Z2/A2)
steps.purpose: Determine whether the Machine Data values that “should match” are consistent between machines for the same axis.
steps.instruction: Compare the Machine Data values between machines for the selected axis. The following data values should match between machines: ID 0 Axis Name, ID 1 OT Minus, ID 5 Tote Pickup Position, ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 8 Tote Dump Position, ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos, ID 10 OT Pos, ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle (steps/min), ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (steps/min^2)/10, ID 13 Jog Speed, and ID 14 Jog Acceleration, plus ID 20 Home Position, ID 21 Home Offset, ID 22 Homing Speed, ID 23 Homing CAM Speed, and ID 24 Homing Acceleration.
steps.expected_result: For the selected axis, you can identify which Machine Data IDs match and which IDs differ between the two machines being compared.
steps.healthy_condition: All compared Machine Data values match between machines for the selected axis, except for the documented exceptions (MD5 and MD21).
steps.failure_condition: Any Machine Data ID other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) differs between machines for the same axis.

actions.label: Compare values between machines
actions.exact_action: Compare the values between machines for the parameters that “should match” and note any mismatches.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any mismatch is found for any Machine Data ID other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: From machine to machine, the following data values should match: ID 0 Axis Name, ID 1 OT Minus, ID 5 Tote Pickup Position, ID 6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position, ID 8 Tote Dump Position, ID 9 Soft Travel Lim Pos, ID 10 OT Pos, ID 11 Base Speed for AutoCycle (steps/min), ID 12 Base Acc/Dec for AutoCycle (steps/min^2)/10, ID 13 Jog Speed, ID 14 Jog Acceleration, ID 20 Home Position, ID 21 Home Offset, ID 22 Homing Speed, ID 23 Homing CAM Speed, ID 24 Homing Acceleration.

steps.title: Apply the documented exceptions for MD5 and MD21
steps.purpose: Avoid false positives by treating the two documented unique parameters as expected differences.
steps.instruction: When comparing machine-to-machine values for the selected axis, apply these exceptions: (1) MD5 Tote Pickup Position is expected to be unique for every machine and every axis, and (2) MD21 Home Offset is expected to be unique for every machine and every axis.
steps.expected_result: Any differences observed in MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) are treated as expected and not counted as faults.
steps.healthy_condition: MD5 and MD21 may differ between machines for the same axis, while all other IDs match.
steps.failure_condition: You treat MD5 or MD21 differences as a fault, or you fail to escalate when a non-exception ID differs.

actions.label: Check exception fields
actions.exact_action: Apply the two documented exceptions: MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not treat differences in MD5 Tote Pickup Position or MD21 Home Offset as a fault; they are expected to be unique per machine and axis.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: There are two exceptions for matching values: MD5 Tote Pickup Position will be unique for every machine and every axis; MD21 Home Offset will be unique for every machine and every axis.

steps.purpose: Ensure the matching rules (and exceptions) are validated across all required axes.
steps.instruction: Repeat the axis selection, ID/value location, machine-to-machine comparison, and exception handling for each axis: Z1, A1, Z2, and A2.
steps.expected_result: You have a pass/fail determination for each axis based on whether any non-exception Machine Data ID differs between machines.
steps.healthy_condition: For each axis, all Machine Data values match between machines except MD5 and MD21, which may differ.
steps.failure_condition: At least one axis has a mismatch in a Machine Data ID other than MD5 or MD21.

actions.label: Repeat for each axis
actions.exact_action: Repeat for the other axis selections (Z1, A1, Z2, A2).

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if any parameter other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) is different between machines for the same axis.

healthy_conditions: On VISU_MDS, Machine Data values for the listed IDs match between machines for each axis, except MD5 Tote Pickup Position and MD21 Home Offset.
failure_conditions: On VISU_MDS, any Machine Data ID other than MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) differs between machines for the same axis.

title: Use Hospital HMI "Remove Tote" screen to remove a tote from the system
summary: On the Hospital HMI, scan the tote barcode to populate Tote ID/Barcode fields, verify extract-side position information from WCS (AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, Status), ensure the tote is positioned properly on the extract side, then press CONFIRM & EXECUTE to remove the tote from the system.
when_to_use: Use when a tote is at the Hospital Station extract side and the station operator needs to remove that tote from the system so the required task can be performed.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform the Hospital HMI Remove Tote workflow (scan tote barcode, verify extract-side WCS position information, ensure tote is positioned properly on the extract side, then press CONFIRM & EXECUTE).
safety_notes: Do not press CONFIRM & EXECUTE until the tote is positioned properly on the extract side.

roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Perform physical lockout/tagout (LOTO), remove and replace the end stop assembly, and inspect the opposite end stop for damage.
safety_notes: Perform LOTO of the tipper before removing the side panel (if necessary) and before removing/mounting end stop hardware.

steps.purpose: Ensure you inspect the opposite end stop because end stops typically work in pairs.
steps.instruction: Before starting the physical work, apply the pairing logic: a collision at the bottom often indicates a collision at the top; therefore, a damaged bottom end stop suggests one of the top end stops is also damaged (exception: belt failure).
steps.expected_result: You are prepared to inspect the opposite end stop for damage after replacing the damaged one.
steps.healthy_condition: Your plan includes checking the opposite end stop for damage, consistent with the pairing note.
steps.failure_condition: You replace only the damaged end stop without checking the opposite end stop, despite the pairing note.

actions.label: Apply pairing logic

title: 7.3.9.1 Pneumatic Valve Removal (LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, M8 connector disconnect)
summary: Perform LOTO on the OptiSweep tipper, remove the station side panel if needed to access the motor/valve area, remove the valve cover secured by four M4x50 socket-head screws, and disconnect the M8 electrical connector from the edge of the pneumatic valve.
when_to_use: Use when removing the pneumatic valve at the OptiSweep tipper station requires LOTO, side panel access, valve cover removal, and disconnecting the valve’s M8 electrical connector (as part of the pneumatic valve replacement/removal task).
not_for: Do not continue if the station side panel cannot be removed after removing the nine (9) self-tapping securing screws.
Do not continue if the M8 electrical connector cannot be disconnected from the edge of the valve.
roles_and_responsibilities: Operator: Execute LOTO and perform the physical removal/disconnection steps (side panel, valve cover screws, and M8 connector).
safety_notes: Apply LOTO to the tipper before starting the removal steps.
access_or_tools_needed: Tools: 2.5-mm hex wrench, 3-mm hex wrench, 5-mm hex wrench, 6-mm hex wrench, 3/8-in. wrench or socket, Loctite®
LOTO capability for the tipper (see "Operator Station Lockout/Tagout" on page 2)

access_required: On-site physical access to the OptiSweep tipper station side panel and valve cover area
system_preconditions: Tipper is capable of being LOTO’d
external_references: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout (page 2)

title: 7.3.19.2 Installation: Timing Pulley replacement (taper lock bushing + pulley set screws)
summary: Loosely assemble the taper lock bushing into the timing pulley and align all three holes. Thread set screws into the two opposite holes (threads on the pulley half, smooth on the bushing half), then slip the assembly onto the shaft with keyway alignment (if present). Position the pulley 8 mm (0.315 in.) from the gearbox pilot face using a spacer and an 8-mm hex wrench. Tighten both opposite set screws in alternating small increments until the set screw torque reaches 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb). Reinstall top and/or bottom side panels if removed, then re-start the operator station.
when_to_use: Use this procedure to install the timing pulley using a taper lock bushing, align the keyway, set the pulley spacing from the gearbox pilot face to 8 mm (0.315 in.), and torque the pulley set screws to 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb).
safety_notes: This installation procedure is part of the Timing Pulley Replacement section. The associated timing pulley replacement figure and removal steps specify LOTO the tipper and side panel removal for access (see related evidence in this packet).
access_or_tools_needed: Spacer (between gearbox pilot face and pulley) to maintain 8 mm spacing
Torque tool capable of 5.6 Nm (49.5 in-lb)
Access to reinstall top and/or bottom side panels (if removed)

system_preconditions: Timing pulley replacement installation context: taper lock bushing and timing pulley are available for installation.
Operator station restart capability is available after side panels are reinstalled.
external_references: Starting The Operator Station (referenced within this section as the restart step target on page 66).

visual_references.description: Exploded view of the timing pulley assembly showing the 1108 taper-lock bushing, set screws, gearbox pilot face, and the critical 8 mm (0.315 in.) gap specification.

steps.purpose: Reach the primary tipper operator control screen after firmware load.
steps.instruction: Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
steps.expected_result: The HMI displays the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
steps.healthy_condition: Visu_MCP_Dual screen is active (operator control panel visible).
steps.failure_condition: Pressing F3 does not bring up Visu_MCP_Dual.

actions.label: Press F3
actions.exact_action: Press F3 to go to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.

success_criteria: After firmware load and controller reboot, the HMI displays the "Visu_Default" screen showing IP and subnet mask settings.
Pressing F3 brings up the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
healthy_conditions: HMI shows "Visu_Default" with IP and subnet mask settings.
HMI successfully navigates to "Visu_MCP_Dual" using F3.
failure_conditions: Gray screen does not appear while holding the top three HMI buttons during power-on.
Controller does not boot normally after power off/on, or buttons are pressed during boot.
Visu_Default screen does not appear or does not show IP and subnet mask settings.
F3 does not navigate to the "Visu_MCP_Dual" screen.
escalation_guidance: If the gray screen does not appear, repeat the button-hold/power-on sequence as described.
If the controller does not boot normally after power off/on (or if buttons are pressed during boot), repeat the power off/on step and ensure no buttons are pressed during boot.
